deterministic_findings.title: Possible hardcoded secret in added code
deterministic_findings.recommendation: Move the value to the secret store / environment and rotate it if it was ever real.

reviewer_reports.summary: I found one correctness regression in the new user-config loader that can crash supported runs when the config file contains a non-table roles value. The rest of the added paths are reasonably covered by tests.

findings.title: Malformed roles value now raises an uncaught AttributeError instead of the documented ValueError
findings.evidence: The loader assumes roles is a mapping and immediately calls .items() on whatever TOML parsed, so a reachable config like 'roles = []' will crash with AttributeError rather than the documented loud validation error path.
findings.recommendation: Validate the parsed types before iterating, e.g. require providers to be a list and roles to be a dict, and raise ValueError with the config path when they are not. That preserves the documented contract for malformed configs and avoids an unexpected traceback in CLI flows that call load_user_config.

reviewer_reports.summary: I found one reachable correctness regression in the new role-assignment path. It can silently assign a role to the wrong seat when the same preset is used more than once in the panel.

findings.title: Role assignment can bind to the wrong account when the panel contains duplicate preset seats
findings.evidence: The role-assignment code records the seat name returned by a fresh one-item build, then reuses any existing provider with that name instead of the actual seat selected by the main panel build. With duplicate presets, the main panel renames seats, so the role can point at a different account than requested.
findings.recommendation: Resolve role assignments against the already-built provider set instead of rebuilding the spec in isolation. For duplicate preset seats, either preserve the exact seat identity chosen during the main build or reject ambiguous role specs unless the user names a unique seat explicitly.
